speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your mucous membranes, and petechiae; to determine the cause, how old are you and have you ever had a normal platelet count or clotting studies before?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP).

The clinical presentation of frequent epistaxis, gum bleeding, petechiae, and unexplained bruising in a 4-year-old male is highly characteristic of ITP, which is the most common cause of isolated thrombocytopenia in this age group. Given the severity of the mucous membrane bleeding and petechiae, I am requesting a complete blood count (CBC) with a peripheral blood smear to confirm the platelet count and rule out other causes of coagulopathy. REQUEST TEST: CBC with Peripheral_Smear
